title: Selection Agent output
description: Merged canonicalization and routing for one topic. The Selection Agent reads the topic's memory.md (source records collected by Discovery) and returns the canonical candidates worth the expensive later-literature Research audit. Each candidate carries its source-faithful canonical formulation, an importance routing level, and a free-form assessment the pipeline appends to the candidate's memory.md as context for the Research Agent. It does not produce the problem's verification contract: the verification contract, verification difficulty, and CI contracts are produced by the Research Agent (see schemas/problem.schema.json).

canonical_statement.description: Source-faithful, bounded task statement. Preserve a broad literature question in source context, but split independently publishable directions into separate candidates instead of compiling an omnibus leaf problem.

candidate_kind.description: leaf_problem is a complete single resolution target; progress_target is explicitly partial progress toward a broader source question.

resolution_claim.description: One sentence stating what proposition would be established or refuted when this candidate is resolved.

decomposition_rationale.description: Why this is one resolution target rather than an omnibus research program; explain any split from a broader source question.

importance_level.description: Only high or medium importance proceeds to the expensive later-literature Research audit, so this is a real gate with downstream consequences, not a decorative label.

assessment.description: Free-form screening narrative appended to the candidate's memory.md for the Research Agent: why the candidate matters, what solving it would change, and any scope or named-problem concerns (including alignment with an authoritative formulation). This is context for the next stage, not a machine-consumed contract.
